images.title: A door at the mean
images.purpose: Show that a door built at the family's mean height makes the tallest members bend, so the maximum decides the door.
images.composition: Six flat standing figures in a sorted row on one floor line, a dashed line across them at the mean, and a solid line at the tallest; white space above.
exact_structure: Exactly 6 simple flat standing figures (rounded tops, no faces) on one grey (#6B7280) floor line, sorted shortest to tallest from left to right.
Figure heights in the ratio 155 : 160 : 164 : 165 : 169 : 173, each with its height written under its feet: 155, 160, 164, 165, 169, 173.
The first 3 figures are teal (#0072B2); the last 3 (165, 169, 173) are reddish purple (#CC79A7) because their heads pass the dashed line.
One dashed amber (#E69F00) horizontal line across the row at height 164.3, labelled mean ≈ 164.3 at the right end.
Height differences are drawn exaggerated enough to see: the head of the 164 figure stops clearly just below the dashed line, and the head of the 165 figure rises clearly just above it.
One solid green (#009E73) horizontal line just above the 173 figure, labelled door taller than 173 at the right end.
Arithmetic check for the reviewer only, NOT drawn in the frame: 155 + 160 + 164 + 165 + 169 + 173 = 986, 986 ÷ 6 ≈ 164.3.
rejection: other than 6 figures or other than 3 figures above the dashed line
the 164 figure drawn above the dashed line
images.takeaway: A door must fit the tallest person, so here the maximum, not the mean, makes the decision.
images.description: Six family members sorted by height with a dashed mean line at about 164.3 that the three tallest pass, and a green line above 173.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Count the purple figures with students, then ask which single number the door must beat.

image_decisions.why: The sorted row and mean line show at a glance who must bend.
